name: Six-panel grid (2 cols x 3 rows)
grid: Regular grid, equal panels, contiguous gutters
reading_path: Z-path: L->R, then down (~94-95% of readers follow it in a canonical grid)
pacing_use: Neutral, even rhythm; dialogue scenes, explainers; the safest default for non-comic readers
limits: Monotonous if every panel is the same shot size; vary Macro/Mono/Micro inside it

name: Nine-panel grid (3x3)
grid: Regular 3x3 grid
pacing_use: Dense, measured beats; slow-time sequences (moment-to-moment) and repetition/variation gags
limits: Panels get small on phones - avoid on IG; good for print/PDF

name: Three horizontal tiers (widescreen rows)
grid: Three full-width panels stacked
pacing_use: Cinematic, calm; establishing + two beats; each tier can be one constituent
limits: Little room for interaction close-ups

name: Rows with varying panel counts (2-3-1)
grid: Each row a constituent: row of 2, row of 3 (fast), final full-width row
pacing_use: Row break = situational change; the short panels speed up action, the wide last row lands the Peak/Release
limits: Keep gutters contiguous so rows read as rows

name: Splash page
grid: One panel fills the page
reading_path: Single image; eye guided by composition
pacing_use: Peak or big Establisher; a pause after a build-up; often placed after a page turn
limits: Use rarely; loses meaning without the build-up before it; splash-as-Peak is an observation, not a tested finding

name: Splash with insets
grid: Full-page image with 1-2 small inset panels
reading_path: Outer (dominant) panel read first ~60% of the time, then insets
pacing_use: Establisher + Refiner details; product detail on top of a scene
limits: Readers split on order - number insets clearly or place them along the Z-path

name: Blockage (tall right panel beside two stacked panels)
grid: Two stacked panels on the left, one tall panel on the right spanning both
reading_path: Most readers go down the left stack first (Z-path only ~31%; <10% at full blockage)
pacing_use: Two quick beats then a tall Peak/Release; vertical motion (falling, height)
limits: Ambiguous for novice readers (they use the Z-path more) - avoid for broad social audiences or add cues (text position, arrows)

name: Staggered gutters
grid: Gutter of the right column offset from the left one
reading_path: Mostly Z-path (~89-90%); deviation grows as the offset approaches full blockage
pacing_use: Dynamic, informal feel without breaking order
limits: Large offsets behave like blockage

name: Separated groups (wide gutter)
grid: Panels grouped by a wider gutter into two clusters
reading_path: Z-path ~71%; the wider the gutter, the more readers read group by group
pacing_use: Mark two simultaneous threads or a time gap between groups
limits: Unclear grouping causes order errors

name: Overlapping panels
grid: One panel overlaps another
reading_path: Layout-dependent; overlap alone has little effect
pacing_use: Energy, simultaneity, a detail popping out (Refiner)
limits: Inconsistent reading order across layouts - test

name: Environmental-conjunction row
grid: Row of Mono panels each showing one character at the same moment
pacing_use: Introduce a group or a shared moment without a wide shot; reader infers the space (common in manga)
limits: Readers less fluent in manga process it with different effort

name: Diagonal / broken-border action page
grid: Slanted gutters, panels breaking borders
reading_path: Usually along the diagonals; external panel structure still drives navigation
pacing_use: Fights, chaos, high tension
limits: Hard to read on phones; keep one unambiguous path and use text position as a cue

name: Right-to-left manga page
grid: Any layout mirrored; book opens from the right
reading_path: Mirrored Z-path: R->L, then down; balloons also R->L
pacing_use: Only when publishing manga-style for RTL readers
limits: Thai and English readers read L->R - mirror the whole layout and balloon order when adapting manga references

name: Three-panel gag strip
grid: Horizontal row of 3 equal panels
pacing_use: Setup -> development/beat -> punchline (or I-P-R)
limits: No room for a separate beat panel; keep text short

name: Four-panel horizontal strip
grid: Row of 4 equal panels (newspaper daily)
pacing_use: E/I - L (silent beat) - P - R; classic gag timing with a pause before the punch
limits: Panels small in a 1:1 frame - consider 2x2

name: Yonkoma (vertical 4-panel)
grid: Four equal panels stacked vertically
pacing_use: Ki (intro) - Sho (development) - Ten (twist/unexpected juxtaposition) - Ketsu (conclusion that recasts the twist)
limits: Qualitative evidence only; works for gentle, conflict-light stories as well as gags

name: 2x2 four-panel square
grid: Four equal panels in a square
pacing_use: Four-beat story or gag in one IG/FB square; quote/dialogue images
limits: Make the Z-path obvious (contiguous gutters); <=2 balloons per panel at this size (craft)

name: Two-panel split (before/after, ask/answer)
grid: Two panels side by side or stacked
pacing_use: Contrast, before/after, question/answer; Initial -> Release with Peak Drop
limits: Needs a strong visual change between the two

name: Single-panel cartoon
grid: One panel + caption or balloon
pacing_use: Editorial/gag cartoon; the reader supplies the before/after
limits: Caption-image relationship must be tight; one idea only

name: Webtoon standard scroll
grid: Vertical strip, 800 px wide (official), images <=1280 px tall, <=2 MB each, <=20 MB / 100 images per episode
reading_path: Top to bottom by scrolling; reader sees about one panel at a time
pacing_use: Max 2 panels on screen; >=200 px between panels in a scene; <=3 balloons per panel, 1-2 sentences each
limits: Platform editorial guidance, not reader research; preview font on a phone (12-30 px at 800 wide)

name: Webtoon scene/time gap
grid: Two panels separated by 600-1000 px of space (or a colour gradient)
pacing_use: Time passing, location change, a held breath; gradient/sepia for flashback
limits: Too many long gaps feel empty

name: Webtoon impact panel
grid: Extra-tall or full-width borderless panel
pacing_use: Peak / emotional reveal; maximises the vertical format
limits: Loses effect if overused

name: Dialogue-before-character reveal
grid: Balloon(s) appear in empty space, character panel below
pacing_use: Character deep in thought; suspense about who speaks
limits: Off-panel balloon must clearly attach once the speaker appears

name: Staircase / zig-zag scroll
grid: Narrow panels alternating left and right down the strip
pacing_use: Back-and-forth dialogue, walking, falling
limits: Keep speaker sides consistent (180-degree rule); craft pattern

name: Carousel: one panel per slide
grid: Each slide = one full-bleed panel, 1:1 or 4:5 (1080x1350), up to 20 slides
pacing_use: Webtoon-like control of timing; Peak revealed on a new slide after a swipe
limits: Uses many slides; first slide must hook; first slide reportedly sets aspect ratio for the set (unverified)

name: Carousel: page per slide
grid: Each slide = 2-4 panel grid
reading_path: Z-path inside slide, swipe between pages
pacing_use: More story per slide; scene changes at slide boundaries (page-turn logic)
limits: Small panels on phones; keep grid simple

name: Seamless panorama carousel
grid: One wide image split across consecutive slides; slide edges act as invisible gutters
reading_path: Swipe L->R through a continuous scene
pacing_use: Journey, walk, time passing across one space
limits: Never cut through a face/character or text at the slide seam

name: Carousel hook / reveal pair
grid: Slide N ends on an Initial (question, about-to), slide N+1 shows the Peak
pacing_use: Cliffhanger inside a carousel; drives swipes
limits: Page-turn suspense is an observation from print, untested on carousels

name: Carousel bookend
grid: First and last slide share composition; the state has changed
pacing_use: Transformation stories (worried -> calm), before/after products; braiding inside one post
limits: Change must be readable at a glance

name: 9:16 scroll-pan of a tall comic
grid: Tall webtoon-style image, camera pans down; 1-2 panels per frame
pacing_use: Turns a comic into a Reel/TikTok; gaps ~270 px (scene) / ~810-1350 px (scene change) at 1080 wide (scaled from WEBTOON 800 px guidance)
limits: Keep text in the 9:16 safe zone; hold long enough to read Thai text

name: 9:16 two-panel stack
grid: Two panels stacked top/bottom in one vertical frame
pacing_use: Question/answer, before/after; dialogue duo (speaker A top, speaker B bottom)
limits: Bottom panel may fall in the UI zone - keep key content above the bottom ~35%

name: LINE sticker (static)
grid: Single figure, transparent PNG, max 370x320 px, even dimensions, ~10 px margin; sets of 8/16/24/32/40
pacing_use: A one-panel reaction; the chat supplies the context panels
limits: No ads, no scenery/objects-only, no overly tall full-length figures; check the live guideline before submitting

name: LINE sticker (animated)
grid: APNG, max 320x270 px, 5-20 frames, <=4 s, 1-4 loops; sets of 8/16/24
pacing_use: Micro-gag: anticipation -> action -> hold
limits: Very few frames; the pose must read at thumbnail size

name: Meme template (fixed form, swappable text)
grid: 2-4 panel fixed layout and poses; text slots others can replace
pacing_use: Shareable formats; form is copied most faithfully while content and stance change
limits: Brand stance must fit (warm vs ironic)
